## Improved

- The bottom bar now uses Material's short navigation bar, so screens above it get the same height in split screen as full screen.
- Shorts' action buttons sit on the same scrim discs as the app's, and the rail, labels, channel row and metadata line up with the reference in both window layouts.
- The Subscribe button on a Short now uses Material's compact size, so it matches the reference's height.
- The comments sheet on a Short is a flat full width panel with a drag handle and a titled header, sits above the bottom bar, and opens at the same height the reference gives it.
- While a Short's comments are open, the reel shrinks to the space above the sheet and drops its channel row, metadata and action rail, so the sheet no longer covers the video the way it used to.
- The comments sheet now rests at the height the reference gives it, in full screen and in a split pane, so its top edge, drag handle, title row and close button sit exactly where the reference's do.
- The music tab heads every shelf with the app's large emphasized title on the same 12dp inset and spacing, and its bar carries four action buttons at the bar's end, so its headings and bar now sit where the reference's do.
- The music tab now opens with the same filter chip row the reference shows, and each shelf picks the body its contents call for: dense tiles for mixes, square cards for albums and collection pages, and round portraits for artists, on the reference's own spacing.
- Subscriptions opens on the same Quick access band the reference shows, on its own 12dp inset and 4dp feed margin, with an All filter row under it, so the channel shortcuts, their labels and the chip row sit at the reference's measured positions.- Subscriptions lists its uploads as the reference's rows: a still one feed column wide, the title in the app's small title style, the channel line and the views line under it, each row 226 px tall at the reference's measured frames (rows x5-795, title x400, channel +36 and views +78 from the title top), with the bar's toggle view mode, search and profile discs landing on the reference's first, second and fourth slots.
- The accessibility dump of a phone screen no longer dies on a title that opens with an emoji: the still's monogram took one char of a surrogate pair, and the platform's XML writer refuses a string holding half of one.
- Subscriptions' parity record now closes on measured reference frames: Home's chips, big title, metadata, shelf header and shelf body measure the same at the start and the end of a run (chips y143-166, title [107,411][320,468], metadata [107,473][320,515], shelf header [64,566][249,593], shelf body [500,876][639,896]), the Subscriptions bar title measures [21,64][163,94] in the reference's idle state and on the port, so the earlier reference dump taken while a refresh ran was the reference hiding its own title and not a frame to match, and the music tab still measures its chip row [0,133][800,197], chips at x38 and x171, heading at 16,224 and cards [16,270][186,491] and [202,270][372,491]. Three reference states have no source in the port and stay documented instead of drawn: the notifications disc (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/components/layout/topbar/FlowTopBarActions.kt:44-53, `FlowNotificationsAction(unreadCount = unreadCount, onClick = actions.onOpenNotifications)` drawing `Icons.Outlined.Notifications`) at [668,48][731,111], the row's more-options button (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/components/shared/card/VideoCardRow.kt:105-110, `VideoCardSideActions(state = state, showWatched = ..., onWatched = ..., alignTo = 14.dp)`) at [748,944][780,976], and the refresh status line (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/subscriptions/SubscriptionsRefreshStatus.kt:20-26, `if (totalChannels > 0) { ... LinearProgressIndicator(...) } else if (lastRefreshText != null) { Text(...) }`) at [21,378][301,396].
- The bar's notifications button now opens the app's notifications page: the empty inbox with the bell on its state card, "Peace and quiet", its body and the Notification settings button, plus the settings action in the bar, all on the reference's measured frames (icon card [337,586][465,714], title [317,730][484,757], body [78,773][723,796], button [274,812][528,876]). Home's bar now carries the notifications disc between Search and Settings, and Subscriptions' third disc opens the page instead of leaving its slot empty. The page draws the empty inbox because the port writes no notification records: the app fills them from its notification helper (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/notification/NotificationHelper.kt:113, `db.notificationDao().insertNotification(entity)`), groups them by day (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/notifications/NotificationGrouping.kt:69-86) and lists them in rows that swipe to save or delete (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/notifications/NotificationRow.kt:44-110), so the populated sections, their swipe actions, the clear-all dialog and its snackbars are not drawn. The music tab's bar keeps the moods shortcut in the slot the app gives the notifications disc: the app reaches moods from a shelf inside the music feed (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/components/music/section/MusicHomeFeed.kt:317-329, `HomeSectionType.MOODS_AND_GENRES` with `MusicMoodsShelf(onSeeAll = ...)`, opened at app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/MusicNavigation.kt:70), and this port's music feed does not draw that shelf, so the shortcut stays where it is until the shelf is ported. An audit of the app's navigation graph against the port's destinations finds no other page the port links to and cannot open: the app's remaining screens (recap, music recognition, equalizer, in-app update, wellbeing lock, donations and the settings sub-pages) are features the port does not implement, so no bar, sheet or row points at them.
- The music tab's bar now carries the notifications disc on the app's slot, opening the notifications page with back returning to the music tab, and moods moved to where the app keeps them: the music feed ends with the app's Mood and Genres shelf, a heading with the arrow that opens the full index over three rows of medium mood buttons in the app's tone cycle, each opening its collection, at the app's measured frames (heading text 187 px wide at the 12 dp inset with its arrow at x752-784, buttons 245 by 75 px at x16, x277 and x538 on a 91 px pitch). The moods index is rebuilt as the app's category grid: the title "Moods & Genres", each category heading on the app's 18 dp inset and its buttons in rows of the app's window-class columns at the medium button height. The music page also remembers where it was scrolled, so a page opened from a shelf or the index returns to the same place the app returns to. One gap stays open with its source: the app plans and shuffles its music section order every session (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/EnhancedMusicScreen.kt:116-152), while the port draws the response's own order and puts the moods shelf after it.
- A mood's own page now draws its shelves the way the app's browse page does. Every shelf that is not made only of songs is a lane of square collection cards at the app's grid size, with the emphasized title eight pixels under the artwork and the byline under it, and an artist's card takes the artist's cookie shape with a centred name; a shelf made only of songs is a lane of four compact rows, segmented down each column, at the app's 360 dp column cap with 48 dp of the next column in view (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/YouTubeBrowseScreen.kt:127-145, ui/components/music/section/MusicShelf.kt:52-138, ui/components/music/item/MusicTrackItem.kt:86-235). Measured against the app at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on each package: the mood page header [22,64][54,96] and [74,64][118,94], heading [16,138][219,168], card artwork [16,184][186,354] at x16, 202, 388 and 574 with the fifth peeking at 760, card boxes 16,184 to 16,405, titles [16,362][177,385] and bylines [16,385][123,405], every frame identical to the app's. The shared card also took the app's emphasized title style, which the app gives every collection card, so the music tab's New releases cards keep their measured boxes with the heavier title inside them.
- A mood's page now shows exactly the shelves the app shows. The app reads a browse page through YouTube.browse, which keeps only each shelf's two-row entries (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/innertube/YouTube.kt:1883-1886) and drops every responsive list item, so the "Songs" shelf that a genre page's response carries never reaches its screen (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/YouTubeBrowseViewModel.kt:49-56 keeps only non-empty shelves, and the song branch in YouTubeBrowseScreen.kt:127-145 is therefore never taken). The port had been drawing that songs shelf as a lane of compact rows, which no app page has, so the mood page now keeps the same entries the app keeps and the unused lane shape is gone. Measured with the focus checked on each package at 800 by 1340: Pop opens in both apps with "Featured playlists" at [16,138][200,168] over 170 px cards at x16, 202, 388, 574 and 760, titles at [16,362][171,385], and Chill's cards still match every frame. One data-driven difference stays recorded: on Pop the port's featured cards also draw the artist line the app omits when the response gives a bare artist list, because the app takes a playlist's author only from a segment after a bullet (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/innertube/pages/RelatedPage.kt:237-243); the layout rule is the same, and matching it would mean forking the shared parser for one page's bylines.
- The music tab's shelves now come in the order the app's own planner gives them, not a fixed lead order: three slots anchored by how much the recommendation brain knows (charts, then the mood shelf, then new releases for a brain that is still cold; quick picks, similar to and community playlists for a mature one; otherwise quick picks, community playlists and daily discover), then every other slot in its listed order shuffled with that session's seed, exactly as the app builds it (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/EnhancedMusicScreen.kt:116-152 over the slot order in ui/components/music/section/HomeSectionType.kt:3-21). This port keeps no listening model, so it stays at the cold start the app's plan calls cold_start, and it draws its seed once per session the way the app does (ui/screens/music/MusicViewModel.kt:1481). The response's own shelves keep the response's order inside the single slot the app gives them, and the artists shelf the app always draws ahead of the plan stays ahead of it. Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on each package: the app's session, which planned its charts first, runs Charts in United States [16,1179][256,1209], Top artists in United States [16,1165][295,1195], Mood and Genres [16,839][203,869], New releases [16,1158][156,1188] and then the shuffled slots (India's biggest hits [16,975][211,1005], Today's Global Hits [16,726][215,756], Popular artists [16,1009][167,1039], Pop mix [16,245][98,275], Rock mix [16,528][107,558], Top Albums [16,811][138,841], Quick picks [16,1091][134,1121]); the port follows the same plan for the slots it can fill, opening with Charts in United States [16,224][256,254], then Mood and Genres [16,713][203,743] and New releases [16,921][156,951] and then its shuffled slot, which was India's biggest hits [16,827][211,857] on one launch and Trending community playlists [16,827][317,857] on the next. The music tab's first heading therefore moves from "New releases" to "Mood and Genres", which is the app's cold-start order; the heading slot, the chip row, the bar and the cards keep their frames. The two apps' whole sequences cannot coincide: the plan's seed is the clock at the page's view model being built (ui/screens/music/MusicViewModel.kt:1481), so two launches of the app disagree with each other too, and the rest of the app's slots are filled from its own library and brain rather than from the response.
- The music tab's remaining differences from the app are recorded with their sources instead of drawn. The section order itself is the app's plan, but its seed is the clock read once when the page's view model is built (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/MusicViewModel.kt:1481, `val sessionSeed: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()` in `MusicUiState`, consumed by app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/EnhancedMusicScreen.kt:115-151 as `anchored + dynamicPool.shuffled(Random(uiState.sessionSeed))`), so even two launches of the app itself do not agree with each other. The shelves that never reach the port are the ones the app builds from its own listening model rather than from the response: the taste rank behind speed dial (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/MusicViewModel.kt:194-207, `_uiState.map { Triple(it.history, it.forYouTracks, it.listenAgain) }` through `musicBrain.rankTracks`; the port pools the same three inputs it can source, `FeedLoaders.kt:581-621`, and keeps history-first order), on repeat (MusicViewModel.kt:513, `val onRepeat = musicBrain.onRepeatShelf()`), listen again and long listens (MusicViewModel.kt:1219-1226, `sections.find { it.title.contains("Listen again", true) ... }?.tracks`), and the maturity that picks the anchors in the first place (MusicViewModel.kt:636-639, `runCatching { musicBrain.tasteProfile().maturity }`). The Charts slot is implemented and measured, including the "Trending" song lane that heads it. The port asks the app's own chart page (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/innertube/YouTube.kt:367`, `charts(country)` browsing `FEmusic_charts` with the app's `ggMGCgQIgAQ%3D` params and its country form data, read through `ChartsPage`), and carries the ranked playlists and ranked artists into the music feed (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/feed/FeedLoaders.kt:570` `loadMusicCharts`, `chartSections` at :591, the slot itself at :555, `MusicHomeSlot.CHARTS -> charts`), drawing the playlists as the card shelf and the artists as the portrait shelf the rest of the page already uses. The lane draws the same songs the app draws, from the same fallback: the app maps the chart page's ranked songs when it carries any and otherwise asks its music service, which tries the music home's songs and then a song search for its first trending query (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/MusicViewModel.kt:641-667 over app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/data/music/YouTubeMusicService.kt:67-96 and app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/data/newmusic/InnertubeMusicService.kt:45-58, the query list at YouTubeMusicService.kt:55-61). The chart page this device and locale receive carries no song section (the port logs it as Video charts, Genres and Top artists only) and the music home answers with playlist cards only, so both apps end on that search, which is why their rows agree. The port's lane is `MusicSectionShape.RankedLane` (`FeedLoaders.kt:381`) drawn by `MusicRankedLane` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/MusicSectionBodies.kt:143`): 20 tracks (`MUSIC_CHART_TRACKS` at `FeedLoaders.kt:563`) in columns of four 320 dp rows 64 dp tall on a 2 dp gap with columns 8 dp apart, a rank in a 26 dp box at the 12 dp inset with #1 to #3 in primary, 48 dp artwork and a 16 dp text gap, a `bodyLargeEmphasized` title and a `bodySmall` byline carrying the artists, the explicit badge and the length after a bullet (`chartLaneByline` at `MusicSectionBodies.kt:229`). Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on each package: both apps head the block "Trending" with a 92 px wide heading box (port [16,224][108,254], app [16,768][108,798]); the first lane column is [16,270][442,355] on the port and [16,814][442,899] in the app, the second column [453,270][800,355] and [453,814][800,899], the lane box 349 px tall in both, rank boxes [32,304][51,322] and [32,848][51,866], artwork [67,281][131,345] and [67,825][131,888], titles [152,289][249,316] and [152,831][249,858], bylines [152,316][390,336] and [152,863][390,883], and the rows 88 px apart down each column in both. Both lanes open with #1 Deewane (Navaan Sandhu, Bir, Daaku, 3:27), #2 Just Keep Watching (From F1 The Movie) (Tate McRae, 2:23), #3 Ishqa Ve (Zeeshan Ali, 3:28), #4 Palayo Sa Mundo (Jolianne, Arthur Nery, 4:29), #5 Beautiful People (David Guetta, Sia, 3:08) and #6 Aarzu (Noor, Khan, Madhurxo, 3:08). The two lists drift from #7 because the rows are a live search answer YouTube reorders between requests: the app's session shows Snake and Ecstasy there, the port's Ecstasy and MASLAX MIDEEYE KOL IKAALAY NEW OFFICIAL MUSIC VIDEO 2025. "Charts in United States" follows the lane (port [16,635][256,665], app [16,1179][256,1209], both 240 px wide) over 170 px cards with each card's title and its "YouTube Charts" byline under it (port card titles [16,859][186,882] and bylines [16,882][130,902]) and the same leading order, Top 100 Live Performances - United States, Trending 20 United States, Daily Top Music Videos - United States, Top 100 Music Videos United States. The fifth card differs (Top 50 Jazz Music Videos United States on the port against Top 50 Country & Americana Music Videos United States in the app) because the chart page picks that genre server-side; the card's shape and position are the same in both. "Top artists in United States" closes the slot with the same names in the same order on both (Drake, YoungBoy Never Broke Again, Fuerza Regida, Bad Bunny, Lil Baby), each under a 112 px portrait with the name box [16,676][128,696] on the port ([16,1087][128,1107] at this scroll) and [16,1164][128,1187] in the app, the heading [16,918][295,948] on the port. The slot's cold-start place is unchanged: the music feed opens with Charts (Trending, then Charts in United States, then Top artists in United States), then Mood and Genres, then New releases, and the lane's own heading does not move the chip row, the bar or the Home and Subscriptions frames. Everything else moves with the response: the app's session carried Quick picks, Top Albums, Mixed for you, Popular artists, Popular Artists mix, Pop mix, Rock mix, Your Daily Discover, Hindi Hits and Energize Vibes while the port's carried India's biggest hits, Today's Global Hits, Band Baaja Baraat, Old School Romance, Divine Tunes and Time to Sweat, and the port draws whatever titles its response sends (shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/feed/FeedLoaders.kt:535-551). Where both answered with the same shelves the two apps kept the same relative order at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on each package: Mood and Genres, then New releases, then India's biggest hits, Today's Global Hits and Band Baaja Baraat. The featured-playlist byline recorded from the genre-page pass does not show up as a card difference on re-measurement: on the Chill page, reached from the moods shelf in each app, the first card reads Coffee Shop Blend with its YouTube Music byline at the same frames on both ([16,362][177,385] title, [16,385][123,405] byline), and a mood's page and a genre's page are the same browse answer drawn by the same converter, so no byline gap is left to align in the port's code.
- The music tab's feed now draws the shelves the app draws above and after its charts: Speed dial, the response's Quick picks and Trending songs for you lanes, and Top Albums. The cause of the missing shelves was not the discarded visitor: with a visitor set and with the site's live WEB_REMIX version the music home still answers the same two playlist carousels, because every later shelf the app shows arrives in the home page's continuation answers, and the port's continuation reader kept only two-row carousels and dropped their responsive list rows and album grids (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/innertube/YouTube.kt:258`, now mapping carousels with `HomePage.Section.fromMusicCarouselShelfRenderer(..., chipPage = true)` and `fromGridRenderer` exactly as the first page at :240-248 does). Two app shelves the port never drew are added from the app's own sources: Speed dial from the port's own music listening history, newest first, 18 tiles at most (`FeedLoaders.kt:574`, `MUSIC_SPEED_DIAL_TRACKS` at :608) drawn with the existing compact tile grid (`MusicSectionBodies.kt:268`, three 64 dp rows on 8 dp gaps, the app's `SpeedDialSection.kt:55-58`), and Top Albums from YouTube Music's new releases albums page, which is where the app reads it (`YouTube.kt:367` `newReleaseAlbums` browsing `FEmusic_new_releases_albums`, `FeedLoaders.kt:595`). Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on each package: both apps head the feed with the chip row at y154-177 and "Speed dial" at [16,224][127,254], and both place their tiles on the same three rows (tile text at y291, y387 and y483, 96 px apart, text at x117); the port's Speed dial now holds songs, not the vlog channels it used to draw, and it is populated on a cold launch with no playback. Two causes were at work. The first was the source: its tiles came from the global watch history, which is video history, while the app keeps a music-only history and adds two pools to it. The app's pool is `(history + forYouTracks + listenAgain).audioMusicOnly().take(40)` ranked by `musicBrain.rankTracks(pool, "heavy_rotation").take(26)` (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/MusicViewModel.kt:194-207), where `forYouTracks` is its "Quick picks" shelf (MusicViewModel.kt:1204-1212 reads a section titled Quick picks, Start radio, Recommended or Mixed for you) and `listenAgain` its "Listen again" shelf (:1251-1260); the songs are filtered by `isAudioMusicCandidate` (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/data/music/model/MusicTrackFilters.kt:4, a song of 30 s to 20 min). The second was that the port only ever read the home page's first answer, where those shelves do not live: measured with the port's own log, a cold home answers `India's biggest hits` and `Trending community playlists` (plus `Dancing on your own`, `Divine Tunes`) on the first page, while `Quick picks` (20 entries) arrives on the page the home continuation answers. The port now marks the plays its music route starts (`QueueTrack.music` at shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/playback/PlaybackQueue.kt:22-27, set by `openMusicVideo` in App.kt:482-486 and wired at :679-681), records them on `WatchHistoryEntry.music` (App.kt:291-318, field at WatchHistory.kt:19-20), reads the continuation page at music-home load (`FeedLoaders.kt:824-830`), and pools history + the response's Quick picks and Listen again shelves + the chart songs the Trending lane already holds, under the app's song rule and pool cap (`loadSpeedDial` at FeedLoaders.kt:581-621). Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on each package, on a fresh install of the port with no playback: its Speed dial heads `[16,224][127,254]` and draws nine song tiles with their artist lines, `All I Want for Christmas Is You` over `Mariah Carey` at `[117,291][249,314]`, `Sexo Nama (feat. De La Rose)` over `Anuel AA` at `[117,387][249,410]`, `Beat It` over `Michael Jackson` at `[117,483][172,506]`, then columns at x377 and x637, and its tiles are the response's Quick picks shelf (`played=0 response=20 discovery=2`, the shelf logged as `Quick picks:20`); the reference heads the same box `[16,224][127,254]` and draws songs with their artist lines on the same cells (`Chill Mardi` over `Diljit Dosanjh, Bunny` at `[377,291][467,334]`, `Coffee` over `Amrinder Gill, Jasmeen Akhtar, Raj Ranjodh` at `[117,387][249,430]`, `BHABIYE BROWN RANGIYE` over `Garry Sandhu, Savraj` at `[637,291][785,334]`), so the item kind and the grid agree; the songs themselves differ because the reference draws its own listening history. One part of the reference's pool has no source in the port and stays recorded rather than imitated: its `forYouTracks` is not a browse answer the port can request but a shelf its on-device recommender composes (`MusicQuickPicks.selectSeeds` over current track, history and favourites at MusicViewModel.kt:228-241, related lanes at :243-256, with the charts as a discovery lane capped at `MusicQuickPicks.DISCOVERY_MAX_PICKS = 2`, app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/data/recommendation/music/MusicQuickPicks.kt:30), and its ranking is `musicBrain.rankTracks`, a taste model this port does not carry. The port therefore takes the same two inputs it can obtain (the response's Quick picks shelf when the home answers with it, and the chart songs as the discovery lane, capped at the app's 2) and keeps the app's history-first order instead of a rank (`FeedLoaders.kt:581-621`); with a visitor whose page carries no Quick picks the shelf still appears from the discovery lane. The music home also pays one extra request now, the continuation page the feed would fetch on first scroll anyway, which is the same eager secondary load the app does over its own timeout (MusicViewModel.kt:684-703). The app's "Artists for you" shelf is built from its artist graph (MusicViewModel.kt:542-548) and not from any request the port can make, so the port draws it only when the response carries it (`FeedLoaders.kt:787`) and its former search stand-in is gone: an artist-filtered search for a phrase returns no rows at all (measured: phrase 0, artist name 12). Its other shelves now come from the response: Quick picks and Trending songs for you draw from the continuation answers, and Top Albums draws under the app's heading, measured [16,806][138,836] on the port against [16,1053][138,1083] in the app, five 170 px columns at x16, 202, 388, 574 and 760 (186 px pitch) with the title under the artwork and its byline under the title ([16,1000][186,1023] and [16,1023][186,1043]); the album list's order cannot be matched from the port, and the reason is the page, not the port's reader: both apps read the same browse id with the same reader (port shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/innertube/YouTube.kt:367-391, app app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/innertube/YouTube.kt:1800-1814, both `FEmusic_new_releases_albums` through `singleColumnBrowseResultsRenderer.tabs.first().tabRenderer.content.sectionListRenderer.contents.first().gridRenderer.items`) and each visitor gets the same 139 albums in a different order, which the server recomposes between requests: the port's two launches minutes apart opened with "Jailer 2 (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack), No Favours, K., Piyawa Hamar" and then "Jailer 2 (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack), Badmash Banayib Raja Ke, No Favours, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album (Deluxe Edition)" while the app's shelf opened with "Midnight in Paris, Tu Mo Kedara Mun To Gouri Serial BGM 1, Jailer 2 (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack), Pyaar Hai, Fuck 9 to 5" on both of its launches; the sets are the same list, since the port's grid also contains "Midnight in Paris" and "Tu Mo Kedara Mun To Gouri Serial BGM 1" further down. Matching the app's order would mean replaying its visitor's request, so the port draws its own visitor's order and the heading, columns and card frames are what it matches. The cold-load order still runs Speed dial, then the charts block, then Mood and Genres, then New releases, then Top Albums, and the Charts lanes (Trending [16,224][108,254], lane column [16,270][442,355]), the Home wordmark [59,65][129,95] with its bar discs at 556, 620 and 684 and the Subscriptions bar [21,64][163,94] keep the frames the earlier passes recorded.

- The port's player page could play, but it could not be stopped or moved inside a track: its surface carried only the queue's step buttons, repeat and fullscreen (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/PlayerScreen.kt:603` `SurfaceControls`), so the only pause in the app was the mini player's, and the platform `PlayerView` controller behind the Compose overlay drew a single grey time label with no bar under it, which is what a tap on the picture revealed. The page now owns its transport: a bar pinned to the bottom of the surface holds play/pause, the elapsed read-out, a scrubbable track and the total (`PlaybackBar` at PlayerScreen.kt:613), reading the engine on a 500 ms tick and writing only a finished drag as a seek, so the thumb stays under the finger, and the platform controller is switched off (`QueuePlayer.android.kt:80`, `useController = false`) because the page draws its own. Seeking is a new engine call rather than a queue step (`QueuePlayer.seekTo` at shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/playback/QueuePlayer.kt:50, `AndroidQueuePlayer.seekTo` at QueuePlayer.android.kt:243). Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on the package, playing `Alpha And Tikawar Were Kicked Off The ISLAND By BODYBUILDER Villagers In Minecraft`: the pause control `[22,403][54,435]`, the elapsed label `19:32` `[69,409][105,427]`, the track `[105,389][748,448]` and the total `24:22` `[746,409][784,427]` all sit inside the 450 px surface above the title at `[16,466]`; pausing reported `state=2 speed=0.0` on the session, resuming returned `state=3 speed=1.0`, and one tap on the track at 72 percent reported `seek to 1118672ms` and the session came back `state=3 position=1130626`. The reference draws the same three things on its own surface (measured in its own session, playing a home card: a centred pause button, the pair "00:32 / 18:01" at the surface's bottom left and a seek bar across its full width), so this closes the control gap rather than inventing a layout.

- A track the queue had nothing behind now rolls into the page's related rail instead of going inert. The engine reports only the end of its whole playlist (`onEnded`), so the decision belongs in the shell: `App.kt` keeps the rail the page loaded (`onRelated` from `PlayerScreen.kt`, set when the watch page's detail arrives and emptied when a different video's queue starts), and its `LaunchedEffect(queueEndedAt)` appends the first related card the queue does not already hold, drops the engine's record with `resetQueue()` and replaces the player page with that track's. Dropping the record first is what makes the transition play: a page whose window starts at a track the engine does not hold is read as a stray page and ignored (`QueuePlayer.android.kt` `sync`, `if (!replace && overlap < 0 && loadedIds.isNotEmpty()) return`). With no related card left, nothing moves: the engine drops `playWhenReady` at `STATE_ENDED` so the surface offers Play instead of a pause glyph over a still frame, and `play()` seeks to 0 first, so the control restarts the finished track instead of doing nothing. Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on the package: `Alpha And Tikawar Were Kicked Off The ISLAND By BODYBUILDER Villagers In Minecraft` (24:22) was seeked to `1462293` ms, reached `state=4` (`STATE_ENDED`) at `1462980` ms at 18:42:03.389, logged `resetQueue was=[yuhxX5dPIy0]` at 18:42:03.460 and `sync media=[PQuXEBhNcR4] start=0 at=0ms playing=true loaded=[]` at 18:42:04.409, and the session read `state=3 position=2946 speed=1.0` afterwards; the page itself became `Lava House Battle Challenge In Minecraft` (27:03, the queue's `2 of 2`), whose transport then read Pause `[22,707][54,739]`, elapsed `0:17` `[69,713][97,731]`, track `[97,693][1286,752]` and total `27:03` `[1284,713][1324,731]` (that frame is the landscape window the test ran in; the portrait frame of the same bar is Pause `[22,403][54,435]` with elapsed `0:03` and total `3:26` on `Deewane`). On the new track pause reported `state=2 position=29023`, a tap at its middle logged `seek to 809535ms` and the session reported `position=809535` (13:29 of the new 27:03 item, not the old 24:22 one), and resume returned `state=3 position=812475`. The next item took 34 s to reach `STATE_READY` (`sync` at 18:42:04.409 to `state=3` at 18:42:38.144), which is the same slow first-buffer the earlier pass measured at 24 s; it is recorded here and not chased, as the pass brief asked. The reference's autoplay path was not re-measured this pass.
- "Artists for you" is no longer drawn only when the response carries it. The app builds that shelf from its own artist graph (app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/music/MusicViewModel.kt:542-548), so the port's graph is the artists its own music listening has recorded: the channel behind each music-only history entry, newest first, five at most, and each name resolved through the music search's artist filter, which is the only source that returns an artist's own portrait (`loadArtistsForYou` at shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/feed/FeedLoaders.kt:657, called from `loadMusicHome` at :812 when the response omits the shelf). The shelf the app names keeps its place ahead of the plan (`plannedMusicSections`, `listOfNotNull(speedDial, artistsForYou) + planned`). Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on the package, after one music track had been played so its artist was on the history record: the heading reads "Artists for you" at `[16,563][162,593]`, the portrait box `[16,635][128,695]`, the name `Mariah Carey` `[16,732][128,752]`, and `Trending` follows at `[16,768][108,798]`; the card drew the artist's round portrait, not a song's frame, and tapping it opened the real artist page (`Mariah Carey` `[27,257][184,291]`, `13.3M subscribers · 596M month...` `[27,296][400,319]`, `+ Subscribe` `[59,354][160,381]` and a `Top songs` list with `All I Want for Christmas Is You` and `Obsessed`). The shelf's width is therefore the port's own history: one artist listened to gives one card where the app's deeper graph gives a row.

- A finished video now hands off the way the reference hands off. The reference's end-of-video path was measured first: it picks and appends its autoplay target about 0.6 s into playback (`FlowVideoAutoNext` logged `setAutoplayCandidates ... candidates=20 target=WAVX4Td4ZKE` at 19:02:16.457 and `schedulePreloadNext appended next=... preloaded=WAVX4Td4ZKE windows=2` at 19:02:17.665), it promotes that preloaded item at the end (`promotePreloadedItem d6mfvYmSKI8` at 19:08:43.157), and its countdown card only exists for a delay the viewer set because the default is 0 (`app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/data/local/PlayerPreferences.kt:2422`, `(preferences[Keys.AUTOPLAY_COUNTDOWN_SECONDS] ?: 0).coerceIn(0, 30)`); its toggle is "Auto-play Next Video" in the player's own settings sheet, measured at `[863,473][1082,505]` in the 1340 by 800 landscape window with `autoplay=true` in its logs. The port now keeps the same two settings, `autoplayNext` (true) and `autoplayDelaySeconds` (0) on `AppSettings` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/data/settings/AppSettings.kt:50`, `:55`, the offered delays at `:36`), written through the same stored record, and every hand-off goes through one function, `advanceToAutoplay` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/App.kt:380`), that drops the engine's finished record, appends the next track and replaces the page; with a delay chosen the shell holds an `AutoplayCountdown` instead and ticks it down once a second before calling the same roll (`App.kt:433`). The card itself is the reference's: scrim, seconds in a ring, "Up next", the next video's name, channel and frame, and Cancel / Restart / Play now (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/AutoplayCountdownCard.kt:49`), drawn over the surface the video ended on, with the transport bar yielding to it until the card is gone. Measured at 1340 by 800 with the focus checked on the package, autoplay on and a 5 second delay: a 20:09 video seeked to 1186949 ms logged `state=4 at item=0 pos=1209021` at 19:26:59.907, the card drew `Up next` / `20 Minute Timer 🧡 Study Timer for Classroom Focus` / `Milli Lofi Timer` with a ring counting 5 then 2 and the three actions (frames at 19:27:00 and 19:27:03), and the tick logged `resetQueue was=[CBvqJj8XCxQ]` at 19:27:05.455, `sync media=[It89tBla9lE] start=0 at=0ms playing=true loaded=[]` at 19:27:05.914, `state=2 at item=0 pos=0` at 19:27:05.932 and `state=3 at item=0 pos=0` at 19:27:06.649, with the page becoming that video at `20 Minute Timer 🧡 Study Timer for Classroom Focus`, `2 of 2`, `0:00`. With autoplay switched off the same video ended at `state=4 at item=0 pos=1216635` at 19:35:02.700 with no `resetQueue`, the session going idle at the end position and the page staying on the finished video with Play offered; the stored record read back `{"appearance":"SYSTEM","autoplayNext":false,"autoplayDelaySeconds":5}` after a force-stop and relaunch, and the relaunched app restored that session with no countdown, so the toggle and the delay both persist the way the reference's do.

- The next video stopped starting from a cold request. The 34 s the last pass measured was the port's own doing: it resolved nothing ahead of the hand-off, so the new page began a fresh player request, a fresh stream resolution and a cold first buffer after the queue had already been swapped. The reference avoids that by appending its preloaded item to the timeline, and the port now does the equivalent: once the rest of the playing video is inside the reference's own 60 second foreground lead (`AUTOPLAY_PRELOAD_LEAD_MS`, `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/PlayerScreen.kt:900`), the page resolves the first related card that is not the playing video, warms the media cache with that stream (`preloadPlaybackStream` at `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/playback/PlaybackCache.kt:16`, the Android actual over the player's own cache at `shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/playback/MediaCache.kt:155`) and hands the resolved stream up to the shell (`PlayerScreen.kt:334`, the candidate chosen at `:349`, reported at `:355`), which passes it to the next page so that page opens the exact URLs the bytes were cached under instead of minting a second, uncached set. Measured on the same hand-off at 1340 by 800: `sync media=[It89tBla9lE]` at 19:27:05.914 reached `state=3` at 19:27:06.649, **0.735 s**, against the 33.7 s from `sync` at 18:42:04.409 to `state=3` at 18:42:38.144 the previous pass recorded; end to playing was 6.742 s in total, 5 of which are the countdown delay the test set. The transport that shipped last pass still holds on the new item: on `It89tBla9lE` the pause control reported `state=2 position=89121`, a drag on the track logged `seek to 487703ms` with `state=2 at item=0 pos=487703` then `state=3 at item=0 pos=487703`, and the position was 8:07 of the new 20:16 item rather than anywhere in the old one. The platform controller stays off (`shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/playback/QueuePlayer.android.kt:80`, `useController = false`): the frames show only the page's own bar and buttons over the picture, and no grey platform time label appears at any point of the sequence.

- The next gap on this record was that playback settings had no home on the player: the reference keeps its autoplay toggle, its countdown delay and its loop control behind a gear on the player surface itself (`app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/components/videoplayer/overlay/...` settings sheet, measured "Auto-play Next Video" at `[863,473][1082,505]` and "Playback Speed" / "Loop video" / "Audio Track" rows around it), while the port only had a repeat button and, after this pass, the app's Settings page. The surface controls now carry that gear (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/PlayerScreen.kt`, the sheet opened from `SurfaceControls`), and it opens a "Playback settings" sheet with Loop video, Autoplay next video and the autoplay delay rows (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/PlayerSettingsSheet.kt:51`), reading and writing the same stored settings the Settings page does (`SettingsScreen.kt:138`). Measured at 1340 by 800 with the focus checked on the package: the gear sits between the repeat and fullscreen discs at `[1191,32][1223,64]`, the sheet spans `[244,400][1096,800]` with "Playback settings" at `[260,482][1016,509]`, "Loop video" at `[265,546][378,578]`, "Autoplay next video" at `[265,642][467,674]` and "Autoplay delay" at `[260,740][384,763]` over "Off (switch at once)" at `[319,790][523,800]`; tapping the autoplay row flipped the stored record from `"autoplayNext":true` to `false` and back, and the row's own state line read `Play a suggested video when the queue runs out · Off` while it was off. One deliberate difference is recorded with its reason: the switches in this sheet are not pinned to the row's trailing edge, because the player's own surface draws above that edge on this device (the video's frame was measured covering the sheet from x≈916 at the row's height, which hid the first draft's trailing switches entirely), so the sheet prints each row's state beside its name and keeps the whole row as the switch; the Settings page, which has no video behind it, keeps Material's trailing switch.

- The notifications inbox was the next gap on this record: it drew only the empty state because the port wrote no notification records, while the reference fills the page from its subscription check (`app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/notification/SubscriptionCheckWorker.kt:284-332` reads each channel's RSS, `ChannelRssParser.newEntriesSince` at `app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/data/subscriptions/ChannelRssParser.kt:165-176` returns the entries published after the channel's last recorded video and `SubscriptionNotifications.showSubscriptionUpdates` at `app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/notification/SubscriptionNotifications.kt:36-60` stores one `NotificationEntity` per new upload, `notification:113` in `NotificationHelper.storeNotification`). The port now announces from the check it already has: `ChannelUploads`/`InboxUpload` and `NotificationInbox.observed` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/data/notifications/NotificationInbox.kt:23-67`, the rule at `:70-118` with the ten-per-channel and hundred-row caps) take the Subscriptions tab's per-channel uploads (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/feed/SubscriptionsFeed.kt:37-48`, built at `:112-136`), the shell observes them on every refresh (`App.kt:646-653`) and stores the record beside the history (`shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/data/notifications/NotificationInbox.android.kt:19-31`, the `notifications` key of `flow_onboarding`). A channel the port has never read only records its newest upload, the reference's own rule for a channel with no pointer, so a first visit does not announce a back catalogue. The page now draws the reference's inbox: the bar's gear and its clear action (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/NotificationsScreen.kt:118-152`), the sections **New**, **Today**, **Yesterday**, **Last 7 days** and **Earlier** (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/data/notifications/NotificationTime.kt:9-40`, the reference's buckets at `app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/notifications/NotificationGrouping.kt:20-27` and their titles at `NotificationLabels.kt:30-38`), each row the reference's shape; a 120 dp 16:9 still, the two-line title, the unread badge dot and "channel · time" (`NotificationsScreen.kt:246-334` against `app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/screens/notifications/NotificationRow.kt:44-110`), swipe-left removal with the "Notification removed · Undo" snackbar (`NotificationsScreen.kt:159-181`), the clear-all dialog (`:352-380`), and opening the page marking the record read while the rows it found unread keep their **New** marker for the visit (`App.kt:1006-1014`, `NotificationsScreen.kt:99-101`). Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on `io.github.aedev.flow.cmp`, after the Subscriptions tab's refresh had read both subscribed channels: the bell at `[710,70]` opened an inbox headed **New** with `Full Set (Official Music Video) | Dhanda Nyoliwala × Xvir Grewal` and its line "Dhanda Nyoliwala · Just now" at `[193,190][765,232]` over its still at `[16,190][160,289]`, and `Jigyasa The Curiosity | Standup Comedy By Inder Sahani` with "Inder Sahani · Just now" at `[190,316][765,358]` over its still at `[16,316][160,415]`, each with its primary badge dot at `[202,236]` and `[190,362]`; the stored record read back `DW9F2jELRd8` and `T0iWKW2i6Z8` with `lastSeen` `{"UCdvPL04EnHCT3zaVFb3xydQ":"DW9F2jELRd8","UC0a6k1PuUJrZMJ01xg_wyHQ":"T0iWKW2i6Z8"}`, the real uploads of the two channels the device is subscribed to. Re-entering the page moved both rows under **Today** with the dots gone and `isRead` true in the record. A tap on the first row opened `Full Set` on the player (`FlowPlayback: sync media=[DW9F2jELRd8]` at 12:13:35.910, `state=3` at 12:13:38.242). A right-to-left swipe of 1200 ms at y236 removed exactly one row (`['T0iWKW2i6Z8']` stayed) and drew the snackbar at `[8,626][392,664]` with its Undo at `[365,641][384,657]`, which restored the row already read. The bin at `[760,72]` drew "Clear all notifications?" `[121,305][279,332]` over "Remove all 2 notifications?" `[121,337][279,351]` with Cancel `[179,377][207,391]` and Clear all `[233,377][278,391]`, and confirming it emptied the list to the page's existing "Peace and quiet" state with the bin leaving the bar. Three reference fields have no source in the port and are deliberately not drawn: a row's long-press quick actions sheet (`NotificationScreen.kt:155-163` opens `VideoQuickActionsBottomSheet`), because the port has no such sheet; the swipe-to-save-to-Watch-later direction (`NotificationRow.kt:100-107`), because the port keeps no Watch Later list; and the `GENERAL` notification type (`NotificationEntity.kt:25`), because every port row is a subscription upload. The bar's bell also still has no unread disc (`app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/components/layout/topbar/FlowTopBarActions.kt:44-53`), which stays open on this record.

- The bell's unread disc closes the gap this record left open at the end of the inbox pass. The count is the port's own record, not a reference-only field: `NotificationInbox.unreadCount` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/data/notifications/NotificationInbox.kt:48`, `entries.count { !it.isRead }`) over the rows `observed()` announces from each channel's stored `lastSeen` pointer, which is the same source the reference's `NotificationViewModel.unreadCount` reads from its unread DAO rows (`app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/components/layout/topbar/FlowTopBarActions.kt:44-53` draws the reference's disc; the port's is `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/ui/NotificationsBellAction.kt:38`, a 16 dp `colorScheme.primary` circle offset `x = 6.dp, y = -4.dp` over the bell with a 9 sp bold `onPrimary` count, `9+` above nine at `:66`, drawn only when the count is above zero at `:54`, and hidden from the reading order at `:61` so the icon's own label carries it). The label is new text with the count: `notifications_unread` "Notifications, %1$d unread" beside `notification_badge_more` "9+" (`shared/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings.xml`). The shell feeds it to all three bars that carry a bell: Home's (`App.kt:1457`, count at `:735` and `:758`), Subscriptions' (`SubscriptionsScreen.kt:181`, count at `:114`) and Music's (`MusicScreen.kt:89`, count at `:54`, wired at `App.kt:788` and `:820`). Measured at 800 by 1340 with the focus checked on `io.github.aedev.flow.cmp`, with the `notifications` record seeded to a pointer older than both channels' newest uploads so the tab's own refresh announced two rows: the Subscriptions bar's bell read `Notifications, 2 unread` at `[684,64][716,96]` with the red disc over its top end, Home's bell at `[620,64][652,96]` carried the same `2`, the inbox opened with both rows under **New**, and Back left both bells bare with `isRead` true in the record; a record holding twelve unread rows drew `9+` on both bars (`Notifications, 12 unread`), and a record with every row read drew no disc at all. The seeding of the record is device setup, since no genuinely new upload arrives during a pass; the count itself is computed from the stored pointers, and the record read back unchanged when the disc cleared.
- Home's bar no longer scrolls away into a blank strip. The header (the shell's bar plus the chips) was offset by the scroll while the grid kept `contentPadding` top of the header's height, and its collapse consumed the drag before the list moved, so a scrolled Home left the strip the bar occupies empty and clipped the first row's cards (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/HomeScreen.kt:217`, the header now held over the feed with no offset, measured `:323`). The reference's own header does slide (`app/src/main/java/io/github/aedev/flow/ui/components/layout/topbar/FlowScrollAwayLayout.kt:110-155` over `BottomAppBarDefaults.exitAlwaysScrollBehavior`), but its feed always fills the top because the list has scrolled past the padding by the time the header is gone; the port reached the header-hidden, list-at-zero state and drew the band instead. Measured at 800 by 1340: before, a 500 ms swipe of 550 px left the FLOW bar and the chips gone with a 215 px white band under the status bar and the first row's titles at y194 over missing stills; after, the bar and chips stay at y64 to y175 and the cards scroll beneath them (frames at 13:52 and 14:04).

- Home's header is now the reference's own, measured before it was drawn. The record's earlier claim that "the reference bar slides away on scroll" was wrong: at 800 by 1340 the reference's bar does not move at all. With the same 250 px slow drags on the reference (`io.github.aedev.flow`) its bar actions sit at `Search [556,64][588,96]`, `Notifications [620,64][652,96]` and `Settings [684,64][716,96]` at rest, mid-scroll and back at the top, its chips row reads `All [38,143][60,166]` at rest, is absent mid-scroll and is back at `[38,143][60,166]` when the feed returns, and its first card's metadata row is `[107,473][309,515]` at rest and again after scrolling back; the `FlowScrollAwayLayout` header the app composes is the shell's pinned bar plus the chips, and it is the chips that scroll away, carried by the feed. What actually slid in the port was the whole header, which consumed the drag before the list moved and left the strip it occupied blank under a hidden bar, and what the previous pass shipped instead held the chips still. The port now carries the chips as the feed's own first item (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/github/aedev/flow/presentation/screens/HomeScreen.kt:250`, a full-span `item(key = "chips")` over `HomeChipRow`), the grid's top padding is the bar's own height (`:244`, `top = headerHeight`), and the bar stays over the feed as a plain `Column` (`:340`), so the cards pass behind it and nothing is reserved for a header that left. Measured on the port with the same gestures at 800 by 1340: `Search [556,64][588,96]`, `Notifications [620,64][652,96]`, `Settings [684,64][716,96]` in all three states, chips `All [43,143][65,166]` at rest, absent mid-scroll, back at `[43,143][65,166]`, and the first card's metadata row `[107,473][320,515]` at rest and again after scrolling back, so the bar, the chip row's height and the first card's top match the reference to the pixel at rest and at the top. Two differences stay recorded rather than papered over: the chip's own outline starts 5 px further right on the port (16 px on the reference against 21 px on the port, `ChipRowInset` 12 dp at `:97` over the same `FilterChip`), because the reference's chip row lives in its header while the port's is a feed item inside the grid's own padding, and the mid-scroll card position differs by whatever distance the gesture flings (274 px on the reference against 236 px on the port for the same 250 px swipe, which is the list's own fling, not the header). The pinned workaround the previous pass shipped is gone, the bell's unread disc still reads `Notifications, 2 unread` with the blank bar pinned over scrolled cards and clears after the inbox opens, and every other page keeps the shell's fixed bar untouched.
